_comment: QUESTION: With engagement on the record: did the wasm arm run at all, and is the doubled cap rate a slower arm or a refused one?
READS OUT: wasmRuns, wasmRefused, plansEvaluated_RETIRED, decisions, worstWallMs, capped, turns, decisive, score

DESIGN NOTE: SCORED ON THROUGHPUT, NOT ON PLACEMENT — and that is a correction to the spec, not a preference. `src/lobster/wasm/differential.test.ts` asserts that `on.rows` equals `off.rows`, and that a REFUSED kernel degrades to the same answer rather than a wrong one; `policy.ts` states it in words — the JS path is the source of truth, so `on` is never a correctness bet, it is a THROUGHPUT bet. The arm is therefore bit-exact BY CONSTRUCTION AND BY TEST and cannot move a placement metric: `score`, `win` and `place` are null BY DESIGN here. They are read out as description and they score nothing. Scoring a throughput flag on win rate is a category error and it comes out of this spec. WHAT IS SCORED, in order: (1) the ENGAGEMENT RATE per cell, wasmRuns/(wasmRuns+wasmRefused); (2) PLANS PER DECISION, `plansEvaluated_RETIRED` over `decisions`, and decisions per second at a fixed budget; (3) `worstWallMs`. AND DO NOT QUIETLY UNDO THE RETIREMENT: `plansEvaluated` is a RETIRED verdict metric (conventions.retiredCounters) because at any budget it is dominated by how much CPU the process got, and normalising per decision does not repair that by itself. It carries a verdict HERE only if BOTH conditions hold — the two arms are launched SIMULTANEOUSLY so they share one machine-weather, and the A/A null measures a floor for the SAME statistic on the SAME cell. Without both it is a broken-arm diagnostic and nothing more. The exhibit is in batch 1: its A/A pair swung plans per decision by +65% on `headline-mix-king` under zero treatment, which is what an unfloored throughput number is worth. FLOOR EVERY SCORED STATISTIC ON EVERY SCORED CELL. Batch 1 reported this flag's anomaly on `turns` against a floor of +/-18.09 that the +21.44 delta cleared by 1.18x, and on cap rate against NO floor at all. N0 must floor `capped`, `turns`, `decisions`, `worstWallMs` and the throughput ratio on both cells this spec runs. NAMING: the extractor emits the per-game cap indicator as `capped`; the flag's promotionMetrics still name it `capRate` and the two do not meet — see the CAP-RATE-GATE-NAME item, which is not fixed here because it edits a gate list.

SCOPE: `headline-mix-king` IS DROPPED AS A CELL, on a MEASURED disqualification rather than a preference. Under zero treatment that board's A/A pair agrees on game length in 5 of 48 games (paired turn-correlation -0.193), flips 26 of 48 placements (54%), and swings plans per decision by +65%; across 14 arm-sweeps of the identical configHash 3749a5dea5e82e99 its cap rate spans 0.229-0.458, and batch 1's two wasm arms are exactly the minimum and the maximum of that spread. Pairing by seed buys no variance reduction there, so the cell cannot resolve a ~10% throughput effect at n=48 — which is the whole size of the effect wasm was meant to buy. See the CELL-QUALITY open item. THE ALTERNATIVE THE EVIDENCE ALLOWS is raising THAT CELL'S n by ~4x, and it is not taken: blocks are a property of the SPEC and not of a cell, so this generator cannot express a per-cell n without a code change, and the spec-wide version would spend four times the box time on the batch's least informative board to buy back its least informative rows. Dropped is the cheaper and more honest of the two. N0 still floors `headline-mix-king` — the generator force-includes it — so a future spec that wants the cell back has its A/A floor waiting rather than starting from nothing. WHAT REMAINS: `null-snake6` is the only cell that has shown any engagement AND is stable enough to carry the instrument (A/A 44 of 48 identical), and `hazard-mix-king` stays as the REFUSAL CONTROL — a piece board where the residency check is expected to refuse, and where a refusal that is logged is the finding. TURN CAP, NOT EXPRESSED HERE: the snake cell runs at cap rate 0.917-1.000, which is measuring a stall rather than play, so the engaging cell is also the uninterpretable one. The right fix is a RAISED TURN CAP (or a smaller board) on that cell. It is NOT expressed in this spec's config, for two reasons that are both about keeping the vocabulary honest. `lib/cells.js` does carry `turnCap` in DEFAULTS and `cell()` accepts an override, but make-promotion-batch.js's `cellsFor()` passes no per-cell options at all — only the standing-experiment path does, and only for `budget` — so the ledger has no way to ASK for one without a code change. And a raised cap would need its OWN CELL NAME: `null-snake6` at a different cap is a different experiment, and cells.js's own rule is that two cells sharing a name make the ledger's history stop meaning anything. So the cap change is carried to the local session as an operator instruction in tools/simworker/COORDINATION-20260829.md, and the vocabulary should gain a named long-cap snake cell before batch 3 rather than a hand-edit now.

GATE: REFUSE THE CELL if the engagement rate wasmRuns/(wasmRuns+wasmRefused) is 0 in the treatment arm. That is not a null, it is a broken arm, and reporting it as a null is exactly the error this rerun exists to correct. PER CELL, NOT PER ARM: refusal happens per partition, the evidence says it is cell-dependent, and a single arm-level `wasmRuns > 0` would have read ENGAGED for batch 1 and been actively misleading. AND WHEN IT REFUSES, LOG WHICH ONE REFUSED. The residency check at `territory.ts:388-416` is ALL-OR-NOTHING and returns a bare `false` from about eight distinct pointer tests — one `-1` pointer, including one from the loop over every entry's `entEarliest[e]`, sends the WHOLE partition back to JS — against a FIXED-SIZE arena (`arena.ts`: memory is created with `initial === maximum` and `alloc*` returns null when it is full). P5R must record WHICH buffer or partition was non-resident and BY HOW MUCH the arena was over. That turns "wasm may be refused on piece boards" from a suspicion into an arena-sizing bug with a file, a line and a size, and it is probably the highest-value line in the rerun.

REQUIRES: A bundle built from a tip at or after the CL7 telemetry closure, so TeamTurnResult.mechanism exists. AND BOTH ARMS LAUNCHED SIMULTANEOUSLY, on P7's 4x5-worker pattern, rather than back to back: a throughput mechanism read from two runs that did not share one machine-weather is not a measurement of the flag. P7 had simultaneous launch and therefore has weather symmetry by construction; batch 1's two-arm pairs rested on the weaker claim of being internally load-symmetric, and this whole analysis turned on separating timing artifacts from real effects.
FLAG-VALUE TRAP: every CL flag parses only `1`, `on` or `true`, with no
warning on anything else. Set the OFF arm by OMITTING the variable, and
check the manifest envAtRun block afterwards. Since the CL7 telemetry
closure the per-game rows also carry the RESOLVED flag stamp, which is
the value that actually ran — read that, not the environment.
